title: Physics-informed generative learning yields experimentally verified single-phase B2 intermetallic alloys
summary: A conditional variational autoencoder and artificial neural network, using physics-informed descriptors of B2 sublattice ordering, generated and ranked compositions in complex alloy systems. Experimental synthesis and XRD/TEM characterization verified previously unreported single-phase B2 alloys, including three Fe–Co–Ni–Ti–Zr compositions, Co19.9Ni30.5Ti38.1Zr11.5, and Cu4.7Co9.2Ni36.4Ti38.7Zr7.4Hf3.5. The study reports that random-sublattice descriptors separated B2 from multiphase alloys more effectively than conventional random-mixing descriptors in these datasets.
ai_technology: Physics-informed conditional variational autoencoder (CVAE) and artificial neural network (ANN)
organization: Central South University; City University of Hong Kong; City University of Hong Kong (Dongguan); Shanghai University

evidence.tested: A conditional variational autoencoder and artificial neural network, using physics-informed descriptors of B2 sublattice ordering, generated and ranked compositions in complex alloy systems.
evidence.unknown: The result is one paper-level experimental discovery program; individual alloys are not counted separately. Experiments validated selected compositions from a small subset of the generated search space, not all model proposals. The authors report several new single-phase B2 compositions and strong structural characterization for named samples; broader property superiority and generalization to arbitrary alloy systems are not inferred here. Synthesis and characterization were performed by researchers.
evidence.ai_role: The ANN learned B2-versus-non-B2 phase likelihoods from historical alloy-composition data using 18 physics-informed descriptors, while the conditional VAE generated candidate compositions. ANN scores filtered generated compositions for experimental validation. The paper reports successful B2 structure confirmation after synthesis, including XRD/SEM and TEM evidence for long-range B2 ordering in tested alloys.
